parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Caller-generated unique key (a UUID per logical submit; a retry reuses it, a new user action mints a new one) that makes a retried request safe (ADR 0011 and ADR 0043, REST guideline section 2): 1-128 printable ASCII characters. Postgres is the only runtime (ADR 0037), so the check is on in every deployment: a missing key is answered with 400 `idempotency-key-required`, a malformed one with 400 `idempotency-key-invalid`; a replay with the same key and the same method, path and body returns the original response plus `Idempotency-Replayed: true` when that answer was stored (a success and a FINAL or OUTCOME refusal), while the same key with a different method, path or body is 409 `idempotency-key-reused`. A RETRYABLE refusal (nothing committed; the cause — a conflicting write, a not-yet-existing referenced fact — can change) is never stored: the key is released, so the same key can be retried and a different body under it is a new request.
